entities.description: Chicago Black-oriented radio station; 'Voice of the Negro' (1963), later 'Voice of the Nation'; 'The Talk of Chicago.'
entities.name: WVON

entities.description: Predecessor station on 1450 AM, Cicero, Illinois; ethnic and African American programming before the Chess acquisition.
entities.name: WHFC

entities.description: Midway Broadcasting's 1979 blues-oriented station on 1450 AM under shared-time arrangement; predecessor to the reclaimed WVON.
entities.name: WXOL

entities.description: 1450 AM, operated by Midway as 'La Voz de la Comunidad Latina,' Chicago's home for Latino independent broadcasters.
entities.name: WRLL

entities.description: Television/video arm operated by Midway Broadcasting alongside WVON.
entities.name: VON-TV

entities.description: The Black community of Chicago's South and West Sides — the audience, callers, advertisers' market, and mobilization base that WVON served and that in turn trusted and shaped the station.
entities.name: Black Chicago (community)

entities.description: 1570 AM Chicago; Todd Stroger and Maze Jackson moved their morning show here in July 2020 after leaving WVON.
entities.name: WBGX

entities.description: Record label founded by Leonard and Phil Chess; owner of WVON 1963-1970; used the station as a music-marketing outlet.
entities.name: Chess Records

entities.description: Black-owned broadcasting company founded by Pervis Spann and Wesley South; reclaimed WVON calls in 1984; operates WVON 1690 programming, WRLL 1450, VON-TV.
entities.name: Midway Broadcasting Corporation

entities.description: Owned by George N. Gillett Jr. and Potter Palmer; bought WVON from the Chess family in 1970; moved it to 1390 in 1975.
entities.name: Globetrotter Communications

entities.description: Acquired WVON (via Combined, 1977-78); ended WVON on 1390 in 1983, simulcasting WGCI-FM.
entities.name: Gannett Company

entities.description: Licensee/owner of the 1690 AM facility (Facility ID 87178); Midway programs WVON under a local marketing agreement.
entities.name: iHeartMedia (Clear Channel)

entities.description: Co-owner of Chess Records; acquired WHFC and launched WVON in 1963; died 1969.
entities.name: Leonard Chess

entities.description: Co-owner of Chess Records; co-acquirer of WHFC/WVON.
entities.name: Phil Chess

entities.description: WVON 'Good Guy' ('The Blues Man'); civil-rights organizer; co-founder of Midway Broadcasting; Blues Hall of Fame DJ; died 2022.
entities.name: Pervis Spann

entities.description: Journalist; host of WVON's 'Hotline' talk show; co-founder of Midway Broadcasting; urged the 1986 switch to all-talk.
entities.name: Wesley South

entities.description: WVON general manager in the Chess era; on-air personality; first-person source on the 1968 unrest coverage.
entities.name: Moses 'Lucky' Cordell

entities.description: Original WVON roster; host of 'On the Scene with Bernadine'; created the Bern Club women's organization; later a WVON executive; known as 'Ambassador of Good Will.'
entities.name: Bernadine C. Washington

entities.description: Member of the WVON 'Good Guys' roster.
entities.name: Isabel Joseph Johnson

entities.description: WVON 'Good Guy' ('The Cool Gent'); first-person source on ratings-era decline and 1968 coverage; National Radio Hall of Fame (1995); died 2016.
entities.name: Herb Kent

entities.description: WVON 'Good Guy'; first-person source on the April 1968 24-hour coverage.
entities.name: E. Rodney Jones

entities.description: WVON 'Good Guy'; Motown-era DJ; died 2009.
entities.name: Richard Pegue

entities.description: WVON newsman; sent to Atlanta for on-scene coverage of King's funeral, April 1968.
entities.name: Roy Wood

entities.description: WVON personality; later creator/host of Soul Train.
entities.name: Don Cornelius

entities.description: Journalist and WVON host; 'We Shall See in '83' campaign for Harold Washington; said WVON went 'beyond and above' for Washington in 1987.
entities.name: Lutrelle 'Lu' Palmer

entities.description: Chicago's first Black mayor (elected 1983, reelected 1987); WVON's information/commentary environment aided both campaigns in timeline-compatible ways.
entities.name: Harold Washington

entities.description: Former 20th Ward alderman (16 years); WVON host for 25+ years; 'Governor of Talk Radio.'
entities.name: Cliff Kelley

entities.description: Chairwoman/CEO of Midway Broadcasting; president/GM of WVON from 1994, chair from 1999; 2024 congressional witness on WVON's information and emergency functions.
entities.name: Melody Spann Cooper

entities.description: Journalist; former Chicago Defender executive editor; hosted WVON morning drive 2005-2008; later CNN/TV One.
entities.name: Roland Martin

entities.description: First female air personality at WLS (1973); joined WVON as morning-drive host in 1982; died 1991.
entities.name: Yvonne Daniels

entities.description: Began mid-1960s consumer-boycott activism in part through WVON; tribute accounts say he called WVON with news of King's assassination (unresolved).
entities.name: Rev. Jesse Jackson

entities.description: Civil-rights leader; had a platform on WVON (via Wesley South's Hotline); his April 4, 1968 assassination triggered WVON's landmark 24-hour community coverage.
entities.name: Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.

entities.description: As Illinois state senator, repeatedly guest-hosted Cliff Kelley's WVON show; HR0201 credits WVON with a role in his elections (framing kept as the resolution's claim).
entities.name: Barack Obama

entities.description: Motown founder; sent new releases to WVON first to test appeal with Black listeners.
entities.name: Berry Gordy

entities.description: Former Cook County Board president; WVON morning co-host from May 2019; left with Maze Jackson in July 2020.
entities.name: Todd Stroger

entities.description: WVON morning host; left with Todd Stroger in July 2020 after the Lightfoot discussion dispute.
entities.name: Maze Jackson

entities.description: Cook County Treasurer; weekly WVON segment credited by the owner with helping return over $300M in overpaid property taxes.
entities.name: Maria Pappas

entities.description: Attorney providing estate-planning education on WVON (per 2024 owner testimony).
entities.name: Ted London

entities.description: Hosted on WVON to publicize maternal-mortality legislation (per 2024 owner testimony).
entities.name: Rep. Robin Kelly

entities.description: Journalist (In These Times); author of the March 1989 'Black Talk Radio Sends Powerful, Clear Signals' article — the key contemporary source on the 1986 talk switch and the 1983/1987 Washington campaigns.
entities.name: Salim Muwakkil

entities.description: Historian; author of the 2012 Loyola dissertation 'The Voice of the Negro: African American Radio, WVON, and the Struggle for Civil Rights in Chicago' — the key scholarly source for this brief.
entities.name: Jennifer Searcy

entities.description: Chicago PBS member station; its journalists (e.g., Bruce Dumont) monitored WVON call-ins; aired WVON-related segments in 2014 and 2019.
entities.name: WTTW / Chicago Tonight

entities.description: Published the 2007 'WVON: Minority Ownership Matters' fact sheet for the FCC's Chicago media-ownership hearing.
entities.name: Benton Foundation (now Benton Institute)
